missing_in_a: Behavior for numeric inputs outside IEEE-754 double range (e.g. 10**400) is undefined in A; an implementer following A would let OverflowError escape
A's isinstance-based check accepts int/float subclasses (IntEnum, custom int subclasses) — only bool is explicitly rejected
missing_in_b: Bundled pytest test-suite deliverable (A's REQ-006/D-01, user-confirmed); not strictly implied by the raw prompt
reasons: Both fully cover the prompt: function, formula, 2-decimal rounding, ValueError on non-numeric input, purity, no CLI/file I/O. Both are testable and internally consistent. B preempts more implementer questions (huge ints, conversion overflow, subclasses) but adds more designer-invented contracts; A is leaner with less scope creep (only the user-confirmed test suite) but leaves overflow edges open. Trade-off balances to a tie.
